title: Client
problem: A 2016 Ionic app where a critical booking journey took 12–20 s.
action: Led the migration to native iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin); moved regression testing to Compose Testing + XCUITest.
story: My manager asked for a benchmark: the Ionic app against native. I ran it and presented the numbers. This simulation replays it.
Speed is only what a benchmark measures. Going native also put the app closer to the hardware, opening the door to wearables.

case.context: The app was born in 2016 on Ionic 3. Moving to Ionic 8 would have meant practically rebuilding it, so the question became: rebuild it on what? Of the 12 engineers on my team, 4 work in Kotlin and 4 in Swift. Launch of the native apps: 30 November 2026.

decisions.why: Going from Ionic 3 to 8 would already have been, in practice, a new app.

decisions.choice: Native, not Flutter or React Native
decisions.why: We wanted to stay close to the hardware, without depending on a layer that translates our code to the platform.

decisions.choice: A redesign, not a copy of the screens
decisions.why: UX redesigned the whole app, and we built the native versions from the new design.

case.hardPart: Keeping the current app alive while the new one was being built. Features kept coming, so the work tripled: each one went into Ionic, iOS and Android. That lasted until the current app's feature freeze in November 2026.

title: API Gateway
problem: High platform cost on CA API Gateway.

title: Services
problem: Legacy .NET/SOAP services with a large vulnerability surface.

case.context: About 120 .NET/SOAP endpoints, published on the old CA API Gateway, with a large vulnerability surface. The project started in 2023.

decisions.why: In 2023 the company had no .NET stack approved for the cloud.

decisions.choice: Old and new side by side, no big-bang cutover
decisions.why: The new services went up in parallel with the old ones, and I switched the routes one at a time.

decisions.choice: Consumers move to the new gateway
decisions.why: I asked each consumer to call the Sensedia endpoint instead of the old one on CA API.
The −70 % comes from the security tenant that Information Security runs.

after.title: Node.js
layers: Node.js containers running on ECS / EKS (AWS)

case.hardPart: The remaining ~20 % is planned for 2027: the native app (stage 1) took priority, and it is the same team.

title: Cache & Messaging
action: Message idempotency + Redis caching; reworked the architecture of a critical workflow.

title: Database
problem: Deadlocks and slow batches on high-volume data.
action: Tuned queries, transactions, locking strategy and stored procedures.
result: Batch 8 h → 2 h; deadlocks eliminated; +20 % throughput.

case.context: A rental platform on SQL Server. The batch processed payment slips (boletos) and bank reconciliation, and took 8 h.

decisions.choice: Go after the cause of the deadlocks
decisions.why: They came from concurrency code that was badly written at the time and from missing transactions.

decisions.choice: Indexes, keys and no more N+1 queries
decisions.why: That is what solved it: the batch went from 8 h to 2 h.
The +20 % throughput was measured with Data Analyzer.

title: Quality, Observability & AI
problem: Production issues that span the app, chatbot and web; releases without a safety net.
action: End-to-end RCA with OpenSearch; Selenium / Postman / JMeter; BDD/TDD; 90 % Sonar gate; Copilot + Claude pilot.

parts.result: Load tests before go-live; coverage gate at ≥ 90 %.
